title: Ola Electric to open Rs 1,000 Cr rights issue on October 22
summary:
Electric two wheeler maker Ola Electric will open its Rs 1,000 crore rights issue on October 22. The issue will close on October 30, 2026.
The company will issue 37.03 crore partly paid up equity shares at Rs 27 per share. This includes a premium of Rs 17 per share. The issue will raise Rs 999.74 crore if fully subscribed.
Ola Electric has fixed October 13 as the record date for determining shareholders eligible for the rights issue. Eligible shareholders will receive two rights shares for every 25 shares held on the record date.
Investors will pay Rs 16.20 per share at the time of application, while the remaining Rs 10.80 per share will be payable through a first and final call. The call is expected to be completed by October 31, 2027.
Ola Electric promoter Bhavish Aggarwal has pledged a 4.32% stake in the company to fund his participation in the rights issue. The pledge was created to fund his subscription, with no shares being sold as part of the transaction.
Ola Electric had earlier approved the proposed rights issue of up to Rs 1,000 crore on September 28. The company had also raised Rs 780 crore through a QIP in June to strengthen its balance sheet and support its growth plans.

title: Energy management platform Ionage raises $1.3 Mn in pre Series A round
summary:
AI enabled energy management platform Ionage has raised $1.3 million in a pre Series A funding round co-led by strategic investors and a consortium of CXOs from energy and infrastructure companies.
The fresh funds will be used to expand coverage to 100% of active EV charging networks in India, improve charger discovery and payments for EV users, and help small and mid sized charge point operators (CPOs) set up and manage station operations, Ionage said in a press release.
Founded in 2021 by Vimal Kumar V and Varun Chandran, Ionage is building an EV charging operating system that connects charge point operators, charger manufacturers, real estate owners and EV users. The platform enables drivers to discover, access and pay for charging across different charging networks.
According to the Bengaluru based startup, it has onboarded more than 25,000 four wheeler charge points and supports over 63 fleets across the country. It has a network of more than 75 charging partners and uses charger mapping and roaming capabilities to connect charging infrastructure across networks.
Ionage said it is on track to process more than 20 million units of energy per month over the next 12 months, supported by monthly growth of over 25%.
The startup operates across more than 70% of India’s charging hardware and connects with major EV charging manufacturers at the point of installation. Its solutions cater to offices, malls, hospitality businesses and residential housing societies.
Ionage currently operates across 33 states and Union Territories and nearly 3,000 cities. It plans to develop and support CPO micro clusters in Tier 2 cities over the next 18 months.
India’s EV charging infrastructure needs to grow more than 40 times by 2030 to meet demand, according to research by CII and ORF. The country will require more than 1.32 million public chargers by 2030 to support the expected 30 million plus electric two wheelers and four wheelers on the road.
Ionage offers products including Nexus, Ionage App, Flo and CASA, along with a Discovery API and business SDK that are currently in closed beta. The startup has also started using AI and ML capabilities for load balancing and energy trading across its charging network.

title: Exclusive: Green SM parent infuses Rs 153 Cr in Indian subsidiary to scale EV ride-hailing
summary:
Vietnam-based electric mobility startup Green SM has infused Rs 152.65 crore into its Indian subsidiary through a rights issue, marking another significant capital infusion as the company looks to scale its operations in the country.
The latest infusion comes after Green SM pumped Rs 85 crore into its Indian subsidiary in June 2026, taking its total investment in the country to nearly Rs 238 crore.
According to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, the board of GREEN SM INDIA PRIVATE LIMITED approved the allotment of 15.27 crore equity shares at Rs 10 per share to its parent entity, GSM Green and Smart Mobility Joint Stock Company, raising Rs 152.65 crore.
The company said the fresh capital will be used to expand its existing operations and scale its business activities in India. The infusion is expected to support Green SM as it builds its EV fleet and expands its ride-hailing network.
Green SM entered India in June 2026 with the launch of Green SM Limo, a fully electric taxi service, initially targeting the Delhi-NCR market.
Green SM is the electric mobility arm of Vietnamese conglomerate Vingroup and operates its ride-hailing business under the Green SM brand. Founded in Vietnam in April 2023, the company has expanded to markets including Laos, Indonesia, the Philippines, India and Kazakhstan.
In India, Green SM is looking to tap the space left by BluSmart, which shut down its ride-hailing operations in 2025. Similar to BluSmart, Green SM operates an all-electric fleet with a company managed model, rather than relying on the traditional aggregator model followed by other established players such as Ola, Uber and Rapido.

title: Tanglin Venture leads Rs 16.1 Cr seed round in debt resolution platform Credfix
summary:
AI-first debt resolution platform Credfix has raised Rs 16.1 crore in a seed funding round led by Tanglin Venture Partners, with participation from Stargazer.
Before this round, Credfix had raised Rs 4.5 crore from K2 Capital, Invstt Trust and a group of angel investors.
The fresh capital will be used to accelerate product development, strengthen its AI capabilities and expand its borrower support network across India, Credfix said in a press release.
Founded in 2025 by Ranjan Agarwal, Neeraj Kulkarni and Ayush Kedia, Credfix is an AI-powered financial recovery platform that helps borrowers understand their debt, assess repayment options and navigate interactions with lenders. Its offerings include debt assessment, loan resolution, loan consolidation and AI-powered legal assistance.
The platform has three key AI-led solutions: Risi, an AI financial assistant; Neytra, an AI call shield; and an AI legal assistant. Risi helps borrowers understand their debt and explore resolution options, while Neytra assists with recovery-related calls. The legal assistant helps borrowers understand legal notices, prepare draft responses for their review and identify possible next steps.
Credfix said it aims to support borrowers across the debt resolution lifecycle, from early signs of financial distress to structured resolution and financial rehabilitation. The platform helps users assess their financial obligations, evaluate available options, communicate with lenders and understand legal notices.
The startup claims to currently serve more than 2 lakh borrowers representing over Rs 4,000 crore in aggregate outstanding debt. Around 40% of its users are from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
The debt resolution and collections segment has seen growing technology adoption in India. FREED, a borrower-focused debt relief platform, raised Rs 60 crore in February 2026 in a round led by Aavishkaar Capital. It had previously raised Rs 60 crore in a Series A round in 2024.
On the lender side, Credgenics has raised $50 million and provides technology for collections, litigation management and online dispute resolution. CreditNirvana, a Perfios company, launched its agentic AI platform Maestro for debt collections in November 2025 and introduced an integrated AI suite for collections and lending in October 2026.
CredResolve, an AI-powered debt collections infrastructure startup, raised a pre-Series A round led by Merak Ventures in April 2026 to expand its operations, multilingual AI and voice capabilities.

title: Med-tech startup Sunfox Technologies raises $7 Mn in Series A round
summary:
Sunfox Technologies, the Dehradun-based medtech company behind the Spandan portable ECG platform, has raised $7 million (approx. Rs 67 crore) in a Series A funding round co-led by Ashish Kacholia, Lashit Sanghvi, Alchemy Capital and 3one4 Capital.
The startup had previously raised Rs 15 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by Venture Catalysts, with participation from Finvolve through the IA Growth Opportunities Fund I and Brew Opportunities Fund, Universal Group, RP Singhvi Group and others in August 2024. It also secured investments from all five Sharks in the first season of Shark Tank India.
The fresh funds will be used for the next phase of growth, including expanding its presence across India, developing global go-to-market capabilities, scaling the organisation and continuing investments in research and development, Sunfox said in a press release.
Founded in 2016 by Rajat Jain, Arpit Jain, Saurabh Badola, Nitin Chandola and Sabit Rawat, Sunfox Technologies develops portable and AI-enabled healthcare solutions, with a focus on diagnostic access, particularly in cardiac care.
Its flagship Spandan series is a portable, medical-grade ECG platform designed for use across hospitals, clinics, telemedicine networks and home-based patient monitoring. The platform enables ECGs to be recorded closer to patients and can flag cardiac patterns that may require further medical attention.
Over the past decade, Sunfox has developed a range of Spandan ECG solutions for personal, clinical and institutional use, with applications across home-based ECG recording, clinics, hospitals, public-health programmes and remote-care networks.
Sunfox said it has expanded its presence to more than 15 countries, while its products have reached healthcare providers across more than 1,800 PIN codes in India. Its technology can also be deployed through a hub-and-spoke model in public-health systems.
The company said around 60,000 Spandan devices have been deployed across India, covering more than 20,000 villages across states and union territories. Its Spandan One platform has been used to screen approximately 5 million patients annually.
Sunfox competes with players such as AliveCor and Tricog in the cardiac monitoring and diagnostics space.
Meanwhile, Monitra Health has raised fresh capital this year for its remote cardiac monitoring platform. Beyond cardiac care, companies such as Molbio Diagnostics are expanding portable point-of-care diagnostics through its battery-operated Truenat platform.

title: Agentic AI startup Desible.ai raises Rs 32 Cr led by Prime Venture Partners
summary:
Bengaluru based AI startup Desible.ai has raised Rs 32 crore in a seed plus round led by Prime Venture Partners, with participation from existing investor Invention Engine. 
The proceeds will be used to expand its agentic AI capabilities, strengthen compliance infrastructure and accelerate product development for the BFSI sector.
Founded in 2025 by Uttam Tiwari and Omkar Raikar, Desible.ai provides an agentic workflow orchestration platform for banks, NBFCs and insurance companies. The platform helps automate customer engagement, servicing, operations and compliance workflows, starting with voice and expanding to WhatsApp, SMS and email.
Desible.ai currently works with more than 40 BFSI institutions and runs over 25 agentic workflows across revenue, risk and compliance, collections, underwriting, service and claims. The company said its platform handles more than 1 crore customer engagements every month and integrates with existing enterprise systems.
The startup is built around deterministic decision-making, with workflows designed to ensure that disclosures, consent and escalations follow predefined rules and remain auditable. 
Its use cases include collections, lead qualification, renewal management, claims intimation, welcome calling, TeleMER and cross-sell.

summary:
Edtech startup byteXL has raised $9 million in its latest funding round led by Elevar Equity, with participation from existing investors Kalaari Capital and the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation. 
The latest round follows byteXL’s $5.9 million Series A raised in July 2024 from Kalaari Capital and the Dell Foundation. 
The fresh capital will be used to expand its institutional network, strengthen its AI and technology platform, and develop new skilling programmes. byteXL also plans to invest in AI enabled learning and assessment, student analytics and personalised learning tools.
Founded by brothers Karun and Sricharan Tadepalli, byteXL works with engineering colleges, particularly in tier 2 and tier 3 cities, to provide technology and AI skills alongside regular academic education. 
Its model combines industry aligned curriculum, practical learning, technology platforms and trained educators within college programmes.
The company claims 7,600 byteXL graduates were placed in IT and engineering roles last year. It currently reaches around 2 lakh students through 40 institutions and plans to expand to 120 institutions and 5 lakh students across 15 states over the next two years.

title: JioHotstar expands to MENA through STARZPLAY
summary:
JioHotstar, the streaming platform owned by JioStar, has expanded its international presence to the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) through a partnership with streaming platform STARZPLAY.
As part of the partnership, JioHotstar will be available as a dedicated streaming destination on the STARZPLAY app and website across the MENA region.
The offering will include JioHotstar Originals alongside their India release, television content from JioStar channels, films and reality shows. The content will be available in multiple languages, including Hindi, Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu and Bangla. It will also include the upcoming season of Koffee with Karan and the ongoing season of Bigg Boss across six languages.
JioHotstar will be available through STARZPLAY’s PLUS plan at AED 34.99 ($9.5) per month. The MAX plan, priced at AED 49.99 ($13.6) per month, will combine the JioHotstar catalogue with STARZPLAY’s sports offering.
The MENA launch comes about a month after JioHotstar expanded beyond India into the UK, Canada and Singapore. The platform launched in these three markets in September with more than 160,000 hours of entertainment across 12 plus Asian languages, covering films, television, originals, regional programming, reality shows, kids’ content and anime.
The platform had also introduced quarterly and annual subscription plans in the three markets, with existing Hotstar subscribers transitioning to equivalent JioHotstar plans.
JioHotstar said its MENA offering will have a substantial Malayalam catalogue, given the region’s Malayali audience. The company is also positioning the service around South Asian audiences in the region, while seeking to reach a wider audience interested in Indian entertainment.
Amit Malhotra, Head of International Business at JioStar, said the company sees MENA as a key market given its large South Asian diaspora and demand for multilingual entertainment.
Maaz Sheikh, CEO of STARZPLAY, said the partnership will combine JioHotstar’s Indian content catalogue with STARZPLAY’s regional reach and streaming capabilities.
JioHotstar currently claims more than 500 million monthly active users and a library of over 300,000 hours of programming across 19 languages.
The company has been expanding its international footprint as part of its strategy to build JioHotstar into a global streaming platform. The September launch marked its first major international rollout under the JioHotstar brand, with the service becoming available in the UK, Canada and Singapore.

The company currently operates across more than 16,000 pincodes and is expanding its quick-commerce network as it looks to strengthen its position in the rapidly growing last-mile delivery market.

title: Chiratae Ventures leads $10 Mn round in photonic quantum startup Quanfluence
summary:
Photonic quantum technology startup Quanfluence has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Chiratae Ventures, with participation from Rainmatter by Zerodha and existing investor Pi Ventures.
The Bengaluru-based startup had earlier raised $2 million in a seed round led by Pi Ventures, with participation from Golden Sparrow, Reena Dayal and others in December 2024.
The fresh funds will be used to build and launch a four-qubit quantum computer in the near term, with the company targeting a larger prototype featuring around 100 qubits by 2029, Quanfluence said in a press release.
Founded in 2021 by Sujoy Chakravarty, Ravi Mehta, Biman Chattopadhyay, Anil Prabhakar, Aditi Vaidya and Sandeep Goyal, Quanfluence develops photonic quantum computing technology for optimisation problems. Its hardware-based solution is designed to complement AI in decision-making.
The company aims to develop a fault-tolerant, general-purpose quantum computer over the next five to six years.
Unlike conventional quantum computing systems that require complex cooling infrastructure, Quanfluence’s technology combines optics and hardware to operate at room temperature. Its optical Ising machine uses light waves and FPGAs for optimisation processing, which the company claims can be up to 100 times faster than classical computing for certain workloads.
The startup’s system is designed to address high-dimensional optimisation problems across areas such as logistics, workforce scheduling, risk management and financial optimisation.
Quanfluence is also testing an advanced version of its system capable of processing 10-25 million permutations for complex optimisation problems, including financial risk management, logistics and delivery route planning.
The sector has been gaining traction amid the government’s Rs 6,003.65-crore National Quantum Mission, which includes photonic technologies among the platforms being developed for quantum computing.
Other startups in the space have also attracted investor interest. QpiAI raised $32 million in Series A funding last year from Avataar Ventures and the National Quantum Mission, while BQP, formerly known as BosonQ Psi, raised about $5 million in seed funding this year for its quantum-inspired simulation technology.
QuBeats, another deeptech startup working on quantum sensing and advanced laser technologies, raised $15 million in its first institutional round in April from Zoho Corporation, Indusbridge Ventures and the National Quantum Mission, along with government grant support.

title: FirstCry-backed Swara Baby Products gets SEBI nod for Rs 1,000 Cr IPO
summary:
Swara Baby Products, a contract manufacturer of disposable hygiene products, has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its proposed Rs 1,000 crore initial public offering (IPO).
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs 500 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 500 crore. FirstCry parent Brainbees Solutions will sell shares worth Rs 300 crore, while Anadya Bon Merchari LLP will offload shares worth Rs 200 crore.
The company had filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with SEBI earlier this year in July.
Swara Baby plans to use Rs 198.2 crore from the fresh proceeds to set up a new manufacturing facility in Madhya Pradesh, while Rs 100 crore will be used to repay certain borrowings. Another Rs 27.5 crore will be invested in subsidiaries Solis Hygiene, Swara Hygiene and KAEHPL for debt repayment. The remaining proceeds will be used for acquisitions and general corporate purposes.
The company may also consider a pre-IPO placement of up to Rs 100 crore in consultation with its bankers.
Founded in 2018, Swara Baby manufactures baby diapers, adult diapers, sanitary napkins and panty liners. Its corporate promoter, FirstCry parent Brainbees Solutions, is also one of its key customers, alongside Piramal Pharma and Himalaya Wellness. The company also sells baby diapers under its Cuddles brand and adult diapers under the Shield brand.
According to its DRHP, Swara Baby was India’s largest hygiene contract manufacturer by value in FY25. It held a 37% share of the baby diaper contract manufacturing market and an estimated 36% share of the adult diaper contract manufacturing segment.
Swara Baby’s operating revenue grew 23% to Rs 1,163.9 crore in FY26 from Rs 942.97 crore in FY25, while its profit increased 18% to Rs 95.58 crore. EBITDA stood at Rs 192.77 crore during the year, compared with Rs 162.72 crore in FY25.
JM Financial and Avendus Capital are the book-running lead managers to the issue.

Over the past year, SuperMush has expanded to more than 1,000 Target stores. It now has a retail presence across more than 2,000 stores in the US, including Target and Sprouts, along with sales through its website and Amazon.
The company plans to expand its presence across retail, direct-to-consumer and marketplace channels while investing in new products and formulations.
For NDude Labs, the investment comes after its recent investment in nutraceutical ingredients company Nutriventia. The firm invests in healthcare and wellness businesses across India and the US.

title: BofA cuts PB Fintech price target by 19%; anticipates strong Q2 for Paytm
summary:
BofA expects PB Fintech and Paytm to post strong Q2 FY27 growth, but regulatory changes could affect the two differently. It cut PB Fintech’s price target by 19% to Rs 1,145, while maintaining a Buy rating on Paytm with a Rs 1,775 target.
The brokerage estimates that PB Fintech’s earnings per share (EPS) could  decline 39-41% in FY28 and FY29 if the proposed rules are implemented in their current format. However, it maintained its Neutral rating on the company.
The concerns follow IRDAI’s consultation paper proposing changes to insurance commissions. PB Fintech’s shares had fallen sharply after the proposal as investors assessed the potential impact on Policybazaar’s commission income.
Despite the regulatory concerns, BofA expects PB Fintech to post 31% year-on-year revenue growth in Q2 FY27, while premiums are projected to rise 35%. Revenue is estimated at Rs 2,115.7 crore, compared with Rs 1,613.6 crore in the year-ago quarter.
PB Fintech’s EBITDA is expected to more than double to Rs 204 crore, with its EBITDA margin improving to 9.6% from 7.4% in Q1 FY27. Profit after tax is estimated to rise 62% year-on-year to Rs 218.7 crore. Paisabazaar is also expected to record 26% year-on-year revenue growth.
BofA believes PB Fintech could reduce some of the impact of lower commissions by cutting call-centre and customer acquisition costs. According to the brokerage, around 25% of its call-centre sales staff generate 65-70% of sales, while 80% of customer traffic comes directly to the platform. The company could also increase its focus on products such as loans and credit cards.
Due to the regulatory uncertainty, BofA lowered the valuation multiple for PB Fintech’s core business to 20X from 25X and increased its WACC assumption to 14.6% from 13.6%, which resulted in the 19% cut in its price target.
Paytm, meanwhile, is expected to benefit from the implementation of a 40 basis point merchant discount rate (MDR) from October 15. For Q2 FY27, BofA expects Paytm’s revenue to grow 28% year-on-year to Rs 2,641.3 crore, led by 31% growth in payments and 44% growth in financial services. Its EBITDA is estimated to rise 86% to Rs 263 crore, while net profit is projected to grow 76% to Rs 271 crore.

title: Sauce leads Rs 15 Cr funding round in kitchen and bathroom brand Lorazzo
summary:
Lorazzo, a design-led kitchen and bathroom brand, has raised Rs 15 crore in a funding round led by Sauce, with follow-on investment from Sprout Venture Partners and participation from Panthera Peak and Alteria Capital.
The fresh funds will be used to expand its product portfolio, invest in product development, build its team, strengthen its online and offline channels, and expand its presence across more states in India, Lorazzo said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2024 by Jatin Luthra and Saurabh Gupta, Lorazzo is an Indian kitchen and bathroom brand focused on combining design, technology and functionality across everyday home products.
The company offers products across faucets, sinks, shower systems, bidets, wash basins, smart toilets and other kitchen and bathroom categories. Lorazzo is building an omnichannel business across ecommerce, quick commerce and offline retail, with a focus on making traditionally functional home categories more consumer-centric and design-focused.
Lorazzo’s product range includes the Intelli Smart Commode, a cleansing WC with a heated seat, electronically operated bidets, an air dryer, ambient lighting and digital temperature control. The product is priced at Rs 58,999, compared with Rs 1.5 lakh to Rs 5 lakh for comparable cleansing toilets from international brands.
Lorazzo offers up to 20 years of warranty on products across kitchen sinks, sanitaryware, mirrors, cabinets and faucets. It also provides pan-India onsite installation and service.
The brand has grown its revenue six times over the past 12 months and is targeting Rs 100 crore in revenue over the next two years.

title: IAN Angel Fund leads Rs 5 Cr round in deeptech textile startup IndigoTex
summary:
IIT Delhi-originated deeptech textile startup IndigoTex has raised Rs 5 crore in a funding round led by IAN Angel Fund. SIDBI, FITT and IIT Delhi Angels also participated in the round. 
The proceeds will be used to set up manufacturing, expand its sales and operations team and commercialise its textile products.
Founded in 2024 by Satendra Singh, Prof. B.S. Butola and Dilip Singh, IndigoTex is developing waterless wool finishing technology and wool based fabrics. Its IndiWool Denim combines wool with denim, with variants ranging from fabrics with lower wool content for all weather use to wool rich fabrics for colder climates.
The company is also developing ECOTEX Wool, a technology for washable wool and poly wool fabrics. IndigoTex has set up a finishing facility in Rai Industrial Area, Sonipat, Haryana, while its R&D operations continue at the Research and Innovation Park at IIT Delhi.
IndigoTex has signed NDAs with Ralph Lauren and Kering Group in France and is in discussions with premium and luxury brands, garment manufacturers, fabric exporters and sourcing companies. It has also started engagements across Europe and cold climate markets such as Australia, with discussions in France, Russia and Denmark.
IndigoTex was among 120 startups selected for Bharat Innovates 2026 in Nice, France, and at the BRICS Summit 2026.

title: Medical tourism startup CureMeAbroad raises $1.1 Mn in pre Seed funding
summary:
CureMeAbroad, a global healthcare platform that helps patients discover, verify and book treatments at vetted hospitals abroad, has raised $1.1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by healthcare-focused venture capital fund SteerX Ventures. Existing investor AIRA also participated in the round.
Earlier in April this year, the Pune-based startup raised $600K from Roman Saini, Himanshu Ratnoo, Kunal Gupta, Devaiah Bopanna, Vikrant Potnis and AIRA.
The fresh capital will be used to expand its accredited hospital network, enter new patient source markets, strengthen its AI-powered technology and build its operations and technology teams. CureMeAbroad also plans to expand into non-elective specialties such as orthopaedics and oncology and explore physical experience centres in key international markets. 
Founded in June 2025 by Aditya Oza and Mikhail Bohra, CureMeAbroad is a healthcare-tech platform that helps international patients discover and compare hospitals, verify healthcare providers, get treatment estimates and book care across destinations.
The platform combines healthcare discovery, treatment planning, pricing transparency and patient assistance. It currently attracts more than 22,500 visitors a month and has a hospital network across six countries.
According to CureMeAbroad, the startup is targeting $100 million in annual patient treatment bookings by FY2028, compared with its current $4.8 million run rate. Its key patient source markets include the US, UK, Australia and Canada.
The company competes with platforms such as Bookimed, PlacidWay, The Medical Tourism Company and Medical Departures.
Vaidam Health is another Indian medical tourism platform that helps international patients find hospitals and treatment options. CureMeAbroad has also received Medical Travel Facilitator Certification from Global Healthcare Accreditation, with its network spanning more than 400 accredited hospitals across six countries, according to GHA.

title: Refurbished electronics platform ReFit Global raises $1 Mn in seed round
summary:
Refurbished electronics platform ReFit Global has raised $1 million in a seed funding round from a UAE-based family office. The company was also featured on Shark Tank India Season 3.
The fresh capital will be used to expand its retail footprint, strengthen refurbishment capabilities, invest in technology infrastructure and build an integrated omnichannel platform, ReFit Global said in a press release.
Founded in 2018 by Saket Saurav and Avneet Singh, ReFit Global operates across refurbishment, distribution, retail and related consumer channels. The company aims to build an integrated ecosystem for refurbished electronics by combining technology, refurbishment capabilities, distribution infrastructure and omnichannel retail.
The Delhi-based company claims to have a distribution network of over 75 distributors, more than 2,000 wholesalers and over 50,000 retail outlets across India. The network gives ReFit access to metropolitan centres as well as Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
ReFit Global has also expanded its physical retail presence through 12 ReFit Xpress outlets alongside its B2B distribution network. Its business spans online marketplaces, offline retail and brand relationships, with sourcing and sales relationships involving platforms such as Flipkart and Amazon, along with other offline and strategic channels.
The company also plans to expand its B2B and D2C initiatives across the refurbished electronics value chain. ReFit currently reports a 92% refurbishment yield and repair capabilities up to L4, including advanced chip-level repairs.
Its technology-enabled processes cover device diagnostics, automated quality checks, grading, post-quality-control processes and inventory management. ReFit said these capabilities are designed to improve consistency, operational visibility and reliability across refurbished devices.
India’s refurbished smartphone volumes grew 13% year-on-year in H1 2026, while the organised segment accounted for around 20% of the market, indicating scope for further formalisation.
Startups such as Cashify, ControlZ, GREST and Budli are expanding the organised re-commerce market through certified devices, warranties, trade-ins and direct-to-consumer channels. Vingo raised Rs 10 crore in seed funding led by IndiaQuotient earlier this year. Meanwhile, Yaantra, another electronics re-commerce player, was acquired by Flipkart to strengthen its refurbishment capabilities.

title: CurvetAI raises Rs 6 Cr pre-seed round led by Merak Ventures
summary:
Pune-based AI startup CurvetAI has raised Rs 6 crore in a pre-seed round led by Merak Ventures, with participation from angel investors. 
The fresh capital will be used to expand CurvetAI’s engineering and technology infrastructure and develop agent based capabilities that can handle more complex workflows.
Founded in December 2025 by Vivek Dubey and Utkarsh Gupta, CurvetAI operates an AI workspace that brings multiple AI models onto a single platform. Users can work with text, image, audio and video models, compare outputs and combine different capabilities within the same workflow.
The startup currently has more than 1 lakh monthly users globally, with India and the US being its largest markets. It has also started generating revenue. The platform is used by individuals, teams and educational institutions.
CurvetAI initially started as a platform for discovering AI tools and prompts. It later shifted towards a workspace after the founders found that users still had to leave the platform to use the tools they discovered. 
Dubey previously worked at Infosys, Microsoft and Google, while Gupta has worked at Samsung and leads the company’s engineering and technical infrastructure.
The firm now works with AI model developers and has collaborations with GnaniAI, Rumik AI and Alibaba.

Founded by Akshat Saxena and Amogh Saxena, the company provides coordinated healthcare services for adults aged 40 and above.
Kinetic Age combines doctor consultations, physiotherapy, physical training, nutrition, diagnostics and emotional wellbeing under a single subscription and care plan. The company aims to help users follow healthcare recommendations through regular support and tracking.
The startup claims to have served more than 600 patients in Bengaluru over the past year. It has delivered more than 12,000 sessions and now conducts over 150 sessions daily. The company has also reported more than 70% monthly retention and an NPS of over 75.
Kinetic Age has crossed Rs 2.5 crore in annual revenue run rate. It uses AI driven care protocols and has a network of 25 providers. Around one in three customers comes through referrals, according to the company.

summary:
Beyond Appliances, a smart kitchen technology company building intelligent appliances for modern Indian homes, has raised Rs 110 crore ($11.4 million) in a Series B funding round led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from Dharana Capital and other investors.
The Bengaluru-based company had previously secured $4 million in a Series A funding round led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from Dharana Capital, in August last year. It also raised $2 million in its seed round led by Fireside Ventures in November 2024.
The proceeds will be deployed towards research and development and the establishment of a new manufacturing plant, strengthening the company’s ability to develop and scale its next generation of kitchen appliances, Beyond Appliances said in a press release.

FMCG major Marico has acquired an additional 24.09% stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals, the parent company of plant-based nutrition and personal care brand Plix, for Rs 1,012.03 Cr.
The acquisition increases Marico’s stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals from 60% to 84.09% on a fully diluted basis. The transaction was completed on October 5.
Marico had acquired a 60% stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals through earlier transactions and had the right to acquire the remaining 40% stake under definitive agreements.
As part of the latest transaction, Marico has entered into definitive agreements to acquire a total of 38.18% stake from the founders and certain other shareholders. The remaining 14.09% stake is expected to be acquired in July 2027, subject to the terms of the agreements.
The remaining stake will be acquired for a consideration to be determined at that time. It will comprise a base consideration of up to Rs 592 Cr along with additional consideration linked to milestones and other terms.
With the latest acquisition, Marico’s aggregate consideration for its 84.09% stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals stands at Rs 1,392.07 Cr. The transaction is being carried out in cash.
Satiya Nutraceuticals, incorporated in February 2020 and headquartered in Mumbai, owns The Plant Fix, or Plix, a plant-based nutrition and personal care brand. The company operates in the health, wellness and personal care segment.
Satiya Nutraceuticals reported a consolidated turnover of Rs 864.31 Cr in FY26, up from Rs 432.84 Cr in FY25 and Rs 155.32 Cr in FY24.
Marico said its investment in Satiya Nutraceuticals has expanded its total addressable market in value-added foods and nutrition and strengthened its presence in personal care and wellness categories.
Marico has also acquired several digital-first consumer brands in recent years. Its portfolio includes Beardo, Just Herbs and Skinetiq in beauty and True Elements in wellness. In 2026, Marico also acquired 4700BC and Cosmix, adding healthy snacking and plant-based nutrition brands to its portfolio.

Flipkart has picked up a minority stake in travel tech platform TravClan as it looks to strengthen its international travel offerings through Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel. The financial details of the transaction were not disclosed.
The investment will help Flipkart strengthen its international travel supply and expand holiday packages available to customers across Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel. TravClan operates a B2B travel platform with direct supplier listings across domestic and international destinations.
Its technology platform enables more than 15,000 travel agents to customise and book real time packages, hotels and activities. The platform also provides 24/7 on ground customer support.
Through the partnership, Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel will gain access to TravClan’s partner network, technology and destination operations. This will allow the two platforms to offer a wider range of international holiday packages with on ground assistance.
Nishant Verman, SVP, Corporate Development and Partnerships, Flipkart, said the investment will strengthen the company’s ability to offer international holiday packages while deepening its travel capabilities.
TravClan cofounder and CEO Arun Bagaria said India is becoming one of the largest outbound travel markets and the partnership with Flipkart will help the company take affordable travel products to more Indian travellers.
The funding will support investments in global supply, technology and destination expansion as TravClan scales its platform. The company will also expand its teams across business development, engineering and destination operations.
The deal comes shortly after Flipkart Ventures backed AI startups Alive and Keploy in September. Alive focuses on AI powered lifestyle experiences, while Keploy develops AI driven software testing tools.
The latest investment adds to Flipkart’s recent investments across technology and adjacent businesses as it expands its presence beyond its core ecommerce operations.

title: Exclusive: QpiAI raises Rs 50 Cr in debt from InnoVen Capital
summary:
Bengaluru-based quantum computing and artificial intelligence startup QpiAI has raised Rs 50 Cr in debt funding from InnoVen Capital.
The board at QpiAI has approved the issuance of 5,000 non-convertible debentures (NCDs) at a face value of Rs 1 lakh each to raise Rs 50 crore from InnoVen Capital, as per its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
According to the filing, the debentures carry a 13.85% annual coupon rate and are set to mature by December 1, 2028. The company has not disclosed how it will use the debt proceeds.
The Bengaluru-based company previously raised $32 million (around Rs 279 Cr) in a Series A round in July 2025, led by Avataar Ventures and the National Quantum Mission (NQM). As per Entrackr’s estimate, the company is valued at around Rs 2,050 Cr or $215 million during the round.
Founded in 2019 by Nagendra Nagaraja, Bengaluru-based QpiAI is a deeptech startup building quantum computing and AI solutions for enterprises. The company develops proprietary quantum hardware and software for applications across drug discovery, manufacturing, finance, pharma, and materials science.
It has developed a 25-qubit quantum computer and is working towards a 64-qubit system, with a roadmap to scale to 1,000 qubits by 2030.
QpiAI has yet to file its FY26 financials. During the fiscal year ended March 2025, it remained at a pre-revenue stage, with operating revenue of around Rs 2 Cr, while its losses increased to Rs 16.67 Cr in the same period.

Lighthouse Learning Group, formerly known as EuroKids International, is an early childhood and K-12 education group in India. Its portfolio includes EuroKids, Kangaroo Kids, Mother’s Pet Kindergarten, Early Learning Village and EuroSchool, among others.
Clifton College is a co-educational day and boarding school in Bristol, UK. It has around 1,200 students aged 3-18 from the UK and more than 40 countries.

title: PhysicsWallah’s FinZ sells Rs 95.8 Cr loan book to Auxilo
summary:
Edtech unicorn PhysicsWallah (PW) appears to be changing its approach to student lending yet again. Its wholly owned subsidiary FinZ Finance has agreed to sell, transfer and assign a loan portfolio worth Rs 95.79 crore to RBI-registered NBFC Auxilo Finserve, as per the stock exchange disclosure.
The portfolio accounts for a substantial part of FinZ Finance’s total loan book, making the transaction significant for PW’s lending strategy.
The move comes after PhysicsWallah had positioned FinZ Finance as its in-house lending arm. The company had earlier said that FinZ would allow it to provide loans to students from its own books.
However, PW later shifted its approach and said it would work with third-party NBFCs to facilitate loans for its students instead of taking the entire lending exposure on its own balance sheet.
The change in strategy also comes against the backdrop of a mixed market response to PW’s earlier lending plans. Investors had raised questions around the capital requirements and risks associated with building an in-house lending business, when lending was not the company’s core business.
FinZ Finance received its NBFC licence in September 2025 and started operations in February 2026. A large portion of its lending was linked to PW’s student base.
PhysicsWallah reported a 24.4% year-on-year rise in revenue from operations to Rs 1,054 crore in Q1 FY27, while its net loss narrowed 30.7% to Rs 88 crore. The company’s online business grew 33.3% to Rs 549 crore, while offline revenue rose 14.5% to Rs 490 crore during the quarter.
Following the development, PhysicsWallah’s share price rose more than 6% on Monday. The stock was trading at Rs 128.1 as of 2:46 PM, giving the company a market capitalisation of around Rs 37,812 crore.

title: Indifi posts Rs 371 Cr revenue in FY26; turns profitable
summary:
MSME-focused digital lending platform Indifi Technologies turned profitable in FY26 despite marginal revenue growth, as a sharp decline in impairment costs and tighter control over operating expenses boosted its bottom line.
Indifi’s revenue from operations increased only 3% year-on-year to Rs 371.1 crore in FY26 from Rs 360.4 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 2015, Indifi provides debt financing to MSMEs, with a focus on improving credit access for small businesses. The company offers loans across supply chain finance, startup lending, D2C businesses, and other lending products tailored to the financing needs of MSMEs.
As per the company, it has served more than 1.6 lakh MSMEs across 400 cities. Including other non–operating income, its total income stood at Rs 386.85 crore during the year.
Being a lending platform, interest earned on loans remained Indifi’s primary source of revenue, which accounted for 87% of its operating income, and increased only 2.4% to Rs 321.7 crore in FY26 from Rs 314.3 crore in the previous fiscal year.
Revenue from the sale of services grew 19% to Rs 25.3 crore during the year. This included facilitation, service fees earned from lending partners and foreclosure fees. Other fees and commissions income also increased 11% to Rs 12.4 crore in FY26.
On the cost side, finance costs remained Indifi’s largest expense at Rs 147.4 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 142.6 crore in FY25. For a lending business, these costs largely relate to the capital used to fund its loan book.
Impairment on financial instruments nearly halved to Rs 55.3 crore from Rs 107.6 crore in FY25. In its press note, Indifi attributed the improvement to healthier credit performance, sharper customer selection and closer portfolio management, which helped reduce credit costs by nearly 40% during FY26.
Employee benefit expenses also declined to Rs 79.9 crore, while legal and professional expenses stood at Rs 18.8 crore. Collection commission expenses, however, jumped 83% to Rs 17.4 crore from Rs 9.5 crore, led by higher costs related to loan collections. Overall, Indifi’s total expenditure declined 12% to Rs 376.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 426.7 crore in FY25.
The sharp reduction in impairment and tighter control over operating expenses helped Indifi return to profitability, with Rs 5.2 crore in FY26 compared to a loss of Rs 45 crore in FY25. The company also said it completed four consecutive quarters of profitability during the year. 
During FY26, Indifi also expanded its portfolio across supply chain finance, startup lending, D2C loans, and secured lending. For FY27, the company plans to scale AI initiatives piloted during FY26, strengthen credit management and expand its product and digital lending capabilities.

title: Razorpay partners with OpenAI to help brands run ads on ChatGPT in India
summary:
Razorpay partners with OpenAI to help brands run ads on ChatGPT in Indiahas partnered with OpenAI to help Indian brands advertise on ChatGPT through its growth marketing platform Razorpay Engage.
Under the partnership, Razorpay Engage will help businesses prepare product catalogues, structure product feeds, launch campaigns and track the performance of their ChatGPT Ads campaigns.
Early participants include Fastrack, Traya, Tata Neu, Rivaah by Tanishq, Shaadi.com, Axis Max Life, Tanishq, Palmonas and Narsee Monjee Institute of Management Studies (NMIMS), according to Razorpay.
The company said the platform will also use an AI agent based on ChatGPT Ads best practices to create and manage campaigns across different contexts. The agent will monitor campaign performance and make adjustments, while Razorpay Engage’s team will provide human oversight.
“ChatGPT is changing how people discover products and make decisions. Instead of searching through a fixed set of options, people can describe what they need, explore possibilities, and refine their choices through conversation,” Nitin Bawankule, head of enterprise sales, India, OpenAI, said.
Razorpay COO Rahul Kothari said the partnership will allow businesses to test ChatGPT Ads without having to build the required expertise from scratch.
The partnership comes as OpenAI expands ChatGPT Ads in India, with businesses looking to reach consumers through conversational product discovery. Razorpay said Engage will help brands manage the operational requirements involved in this new advertising channel.

title: Sales hiring startup Scooter raises Rs 1.5 Cr pre-seed round
summary:
Pune based sales hiring startup Scooter has raised Rs 1.5 crore in a pre-seed round led by Aviral Bhatnagar’s AJVC. 
The proceeds will be used for its product and simplify the sales hiring process for candidates and hiring managers.
Founded in 2024 by Kartik Mandrekar and Saumya Seth, Scooter helps startups hire sales professionals by assessing candidates on real sales scenarios instead of relying primarily on CVs. 
Mandrekar has previously led sales teams at Gartner, Shoptimize and Graas, while Seth is a behavioural scientist with a master’s degree from the University of Pennsylvania.
The platform sources verified sales professionals, assesses them through real sales scenarios and provides hiring managers with a shortlist of three to five candidates. Managers can review short video clips from assessments before viewing a candidate’s CV. One customer has made a sales hire through Scooter in six days.
Scooter currently works with more than 50 companies and has added 14 customers in recent months. 
It has built a pool of over 10,000 sales candidates. 
The investment is AJVC’s first in a Pune based startup. AJVC is a pre-seed fund led by Aviral Bhatnagar. Scooter is focused on helping startups and sales teams reduce the time involved in finding and evaluating sales candidates.

title: Snapdeal parent AceVector lists at 11.5% discount to IPO price
summary:
AceVector, the parent company of e-commerce platform Snapdeal, made a weak debut on the stock exchanges on Monday, October 5, with its shares listing at a discount of around 12% to the IPO price.
The company’s shares opened at Rs 28.32 on the NSE, compared with the issue price of Rs 32, an 11.5% discount. On the BSE, the stock opened at Rs 28.30, down 11.56% from the IPO price.
The weak debut came despite AceVector’s Rs 420 crore IPO receiving strong investor interest. The issue was subscribed around 5 times during its three-day bidding period, with the retail portion subscribed 4.83 times and the non-institutional investor category receiving 8.53 times subscription.
The IPO comprised a fresh issue of Rs 287 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of Rs 133 crore. The company had fixed the price band at Rs 30-32 per share.
SoftBank, Nexus Venture Partners and other existing investors partially offloaded their stakes through the OFS, while co-founders Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal did not sell any shares in the IPO.
AceVector plans to use a portion of the IPO proceeds to fund marketing and promotional expenses for its marketplace business. Around Rs 132 crore has been earmarked for this purpose, while another Rs 50 crore will go towards technology infrastructure. The remaining funds will be used for acquisitions and general corporate purposes.
AceVector operates Snapdeal along with e-commerce enablement platforms such as Uniware, Shipway and Convertway. It also owns consumer brands under Stellaro Brands.
The company’s financial performance improved in FY26. Its total income rose 32% year-on-year to Rs 538 crore from Rs 407 crore in FY25. At the same time, its net loss narrowed sharply to Rs 45 crore from Rs 126 crore a year earlier.

title: Nykaa expects around 30% GMV growth in Q2 FY27
summary:
FSN E-Commerce Ventures, the parent company of beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa, expects its consolidated GMV to grow close to 30% year-on-year in the quarter ended September 2026.
According to the company’s quarterly business update, consolidated NSV is expected to grow in the early thirties, while net revenue growth is projected to be in the late twenties. The growth was led by continued momentum in the beauty business and the increasing scale of its fashion vertical.
Nykaa’s beauty vertical is expected to post NSV and net revenue growth in the late twenties, as per the release. Its retail network expanded by 14 net new stores during the quarter, taking the total store count to 338 as of September-end. 
The fashion vertical continued to gain momentum, with NSV expected to grow in the late forties and net revenue in the early forties. Nykaa said new customer acquisition remained a key growth driver for the fashion business.
It added more than 250 brands across categories during the quarter, while its partnership with Nike continued to see encouraging early traction through exclusive product drops.
Nykaa reported a 29% year-on-year growth in operating revenue to Rs 2,782 crore in Q1 FY27, while its profit surged 3.3X to Rs 80 crore. The beauty segment contributed Rs 2,516 crore, while fashion brought in Rs 253 crore during the quarter.
Meanwhile, Nykaa recently partnered with BOLD, the corporate venture capital arm of L’Oréal, to jointly invest in emerging Indian beauty and personal care brands. The partnership will target high-growth startups and provide them with capital, strategic mentorship, and access to Nykaa’s retail and distribution capabilities.

title: Bhavish Aggarwal pledges 4.32% Ola Electric stake to fund rights issue
summary:
Ola Electric promoter Bhavish Aggarwal has pledged a 4.32% stake in the electric two-wheeler maker to fund his participation in the company’s upcoming rights issue.
As per the filing with the National Stock Exchange, the pledge has been created solely to fund Aggarwal’s subscription to the rights issue approved by Ola Electric’s board. No shares are being sold as part of the transaction.
Ola Electric’s board had approved a rights issue of up to Rs 1,000 crore on September 28. The company subsequently filed its Draft Letter of Offer with the exchanges.
However, the company’s latest statement does not disclose the amount being raised by Aggarwal against the pledged shares or the exact amount he plans to invest in the rights issue.
The move comes at a time when Ola Electric is looking to strengthen its financial position amid pressure on its business. The company’s operating revenue declined 45% year-on-year to Rs 455 crore in Q1 FY27, from Rs 828 crore in the year-ago quarter. Its EV registrations also fell 25% to 43,908 units during the quarter. However, the company narrowed its net loss by 21.1% to Rs 336 crore during the quarter.
Ola Electric had also raised Rs 780 crore through a qualified institutional placement (QIP) in June, after its board approved the fundraise to strengthen the company’s balance sheet and support its growth plans.
The latest rights issue will give existing shareholders another opportunity to put fresh money into the company, while Aggarwal is using a portion of his existing stake as collateral to fund his participation.
The company, which went public in August 2024, has been expanding its electric two-wheeler portfolio and manufacturing capabilities as it competes with established players such as TVS Motor and Bajaj Auto, as well as Ather Energy.
The company’s shares closed at Rs 37.09 per share in the last trading session, giving it a total market capitalisation of Rs 17,162 crore.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Sep 28 - Oct 3]
summary:
This week, 24 Indian startups raised $411.46 million across five growth-stage deals, 13 early-stage deals, and 6 undisclosed rounds. The week also saw 3 key appointments, one fund launch and three mergers & acquisitions and one ESOP buyback.

In contrast, 17 startups had collectively secured about $188.49 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]
Growth-stage startups raised $357 million across just five deals this week. Electric two-wheeler maker Simple Energy led with a $182 million Series C round, followed by physical AI company SiMa.ai with $150 million.
Balwaan Krishi raised Rs 100 crore in Series B funding, while Seeds Fincap secured over Rs 100 crore. Quick-commerce fulfillment startup Blitz also raised Rs 28.7 crore in a pre-Series B round led by IvyCap Ventures.
[Early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups raised $54.36 million across 13 deals this week. Premium home interior materials startup Gravity led with $15 million in equity and debt funding, followed by edtech startup Arivihan with $10 million.
Arovia Consumer secured a Rs 100 crore capital commitment from Fireside Ventures, while beauty and wellness startup Amaani and Bharat Housing Network raised $5 million each.
Other funded startups included EDT, Bangalore Watch Company, Alive App and Vytalyou, among others. FIG Living, Prodocv AI, Nudge and three others also raised funding this week but did not disclose the amounts.
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru again led the funding charts with 13 startup deals during the week, followed by Delhi-NCR and Mumbai with three deals each. Jaipur, Ahmedabad and Hyderabad also recorded deals.

Healthtech startups led the sectors with four deals, followed by AI and e-commerce startups which grabbed three deals each. Meanwhile interior design, fintech, EV, edtech, quick commerce and others also saw funding activity.
[Series-wise deals]
Seed rounds led the week with nine deals, followed by Series A with three. Series B, Series C, pre-seed and pre-Series A recorded two deals each, while pre-Series B and angel rounds saw one deal each.

[Week-on-week funding trend]
On a weekly basis, startup funding jumped over 2X to $411.46 million from $188.49 million raised in the previous week.
The average weekly funding over the past eight weeks stood at around $236.34 million across 21 deals.
[Key Hirings]
Only three key hirings were recorded this week. Bessemer Venture Partners appointed Mayank Khanduja as Partner for its India practice, nearly nine months after his exit from Elevation Capital following a 15-year stint.
Identity and access management startup OTPless elevated early team member Manas Poddar as Chief Business Officer, while Chiratae Ventures appointed Keshav R. Murugesh to its Global Advisory Board.
[Mergers and Acquisitions]
Three acquisitions were recorded this week. FMCG major ITC completed its acquisition of Yoga Bar parent Sproutlife Foods after acquiring the remaining stake in the Bengaluru-based company.
OpenMetal acquired cloud cost management platform Economize, while Zigly Pet Care acquired Prolife Speciality Vet Clinic in Mumbai to strengthen its veterinary healthcare network.
[Fund Launches]
Seed-stage venture capital firm WEH Ventures announced the first close of its third fund, which has a target corpus of Rs 250 crore. The fund plans to back 20 to 25 early-stage Indian startups catering to domestic and global markets.
[ESOP Buyback]
Stable Money completed its second ESOP buyback within four years of its launch, founder Saurabh Jain announced in a LinkedIn post.
[Financial results this week]

 
[New launches and partnerships]
▪️ Apple Pay launches in India with Axis Bank cards; Razorpay, Cashfree and others enable merchant support
Apple has launched Apple Pay in India with Axis Bank as its first banking partner, initially supporting Visa and Mastercard credit cards. The service enables contactless payments across stores, apps and online platforms, with the rollout supported by payment players including Razorpay, Cashfree, Mswipe, Paytm, PayU, Pine Labs, Juspay and Worldline.
▪️ Flipkart expands warehouse capacity by 14 Mn cubic feet ahead of festive season
Flipkart has expanded its supply chain ahead of the festive season, adding 14 million cubic feet of warehousing capacity and extending its delivery network to over 750 new PIN codes. The expansion increased storage capacity by 50%, while automation and technology upgrades boosted peak processing volumes by more than 30% ahead of its Big Billion Days sale.
▪️Actor Ranbir Kapoor enters FMCG with Flux Theory, launches body-care range
Actor Ranbir Kapoor has entered the FMCG space with the launch of body-care brand Flux Theory, co-founded with Advay Jhunjhunwala and venture-building platform Think9. The brand has launched five body-wash variants and will follow an omnichannel strategy, with products available across Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Zepto, Tira, Instamart and its own website.
[News flash this week]
▪️ Indian startups raise $2.9 Bn in Q3 2026 as EV, AI drive funding
Indian startups raised less than $3 billion in Q3 2026, compared to $3.5 billion in Q2 and $3.87 billion in Q1. Simple Energy led the quarter with a $182 million round, followed by SiMa.ai with $150 million, while Emergent, River Mobility, Navi, Slice and Pixxel raised over $100 million each.
▪️ TVS retains EV two-wheeler lead in September as Bajaj, Hero see strong growth
India’s electric two-wheeler registrations rose over 12% month on month to 2.07 lakh units in September from 1.85 lakh in August. TVS Motor retained its lead with 53,989 registrations and a 26.06% market share, while Bajaj Auto and Hero MotoCorp also recorded strong growth during the month.
▪️UPI transaction volume stays above 24 Bn despite 1.8% M-o-M dip in September
UPI processed 24.07 billion transactions worth Rs 29.37 lakh crore in September 2026, with volume and value declining 1.8% and 1.5% month on month, respectively. However, average daily transactions rose 1.4% to 802 million. On a year-on-year basis, UPI volume grew 23%, while transaction value increased 18%.
▪️ Moneyview shares debut at 64% premium after 100X IPO subscription
Digital lending platform Moneyview made a strong stock market debut on Thursday, listing at over 60% premium to its IPO price of Rs 34. Its shares opened at Rs 55.61 on the BSE and Rs 55 on the NSE. The Rs 1,092 crore IPO comprised a Rs 750 crore fresh issue and an OFS worth around Rs 342 crore.
▪️ Smartworks secures managed office deals worth Rs 305 Cr from new clients
Smartworks has signed new leasing deals with large corporate clients across multiple cities, adding around Rs 305 crore in contracted rental revenue over engagements of up to 60 months. The deals take its contracted rental revenue base beyond Rs 5,400 crore as of June 2026 and follow Rs 235 crore of incremental rental revenue announced from existing client expansions.
▪️CtrlS has deployed Ciena’s optical technology to power managed optical fiber networks for hyperscalers.
CtrlS Datacenters has partnered with Ciena to build five metro networks connecting nine data centers across Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, New Delhi and Noida, with capacity of up to 100 Tb/s. The deployment will support growing bandwidth demand from cloud and AI services.
▪️ DraperU India Demo Day: 13 Startups Pitch to Investors; Ordo and WearSynapse Secure Rs 25 Lakh Each
DraperU India concluded its latest Founders Program with a Demo Day in Hyderabad, where 13 startups pitched to over 150 investors and industry leaders. Ordo and WearSynapse secured Rs 25 lakh investment commitments each from DraperU India and were selected to represent the program at Draper University’s Hero Training Program in Silicon Valley. Ordo, WearSynapse and Creator Studio also shared a Rs 90,000 prize pool from IDFC FIRST Bank.
▪️ SUJÁN has acquired Chiawa Camp and Old Mondoro, expanding its conservation-led safari portfolio into Africa.
Luxury hospitality company SUJÁN has acquired Chiawa Camp and Old Mondoro from Chiawa Safaris, marking its first major international expansion beyond India. The deal establishes SUJÁN’s presence in Zambia’s Lower Zambezi National Park and expands its conservation-led safari portfolio into Africa.
▪️ Zelio E-Mobility to raise Rs 168 Cr through preferential issue
EV manufacturer Zelio E-Mobility’s board has approved raising up to Rs 167.95 crore through a preferential issue of equity shares and convertible warrants. The BSE SME-listed company will issue 9.73 lakh shares at Rs 853 apiece to investors including Motilal Oswal Financial Services, Calliope Capital Advisors, Param Value Investments and Hem Growth Opportunities Fund.
▪️ CoinSwitch turns profitable in FY26 as revenue surges 150% to Rs 324 Cr
Crypto investing platform CoinSwitch turned profitable on an adjusted EBITDA basis in FY26 as revenue surged 150% to Rs 324.19 crore. Adjusted EBITDA jumped to Rs 86.38 crore from Rs 1.65 crore in FY25, while its margin expanded to 27%. Operating costs rose 37% to Rs 270.07 crore during the year.
▪️ PayMe nearly doubles monthly disbursals to Rs 200 Cr, targets Rs 2,000 Cr annually
Fintech firm PayMe crossed Rs 200 crore in monthly loan disbursals in September 2026, nearly doubling from the Rs 100 crore mark reached earlier this year. The Noida-based NBFC, which disbursed over Rs 1,300 crore in FY26, is targeting more than Rs 2,000 crore in FY27 and aims to reach a monthly run rate of Rs 500 crore by the end of the fiscal year.

title: Kuku clocks Rs 1,484 Cr revenue and Rs 89 Cr PBT in FY26; spends Rs 1,100 Cr on marketing
summary:
Audio and video content platform Kuku FM’s parent Kuku Technologies saw its operating revenue surge more than six-fold in FY26, backed by Rs 1,105 crore in marketing and advertising spends. The IPO-bound company also turned profitable during the year, posting a profit before tax of Rs 88.6 crore.
Kuku Technologies’ revenue from operations ballooned to Rs 1,484.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 241.5 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Kuku FM offers audio content across genres such as business, self-help, personal finance, history, religion, entertainment and fitness. The company also operates Kuku TV, Guru and StoRizz, offering audio and video content primarily through subscription plans.
Subscription revenue remained its primary source of income, contributing Rs 1,475.4 crore, or over 99% of operating revenue in FY26. The firm also earned Rs 6.86 crore from its pay-per-piece model, where users purchase coins to unlock content, while advertising income stood at Rs 1.9 crore.
The company also earned Rs 26.2 crore in non-operating sources such as interests on bank deposits, which took its overall income to Rs 1,510.4 crore  during the fiscal year ending March 2026.
The hockey-stick growth came as Kuku scaled Kuku TV, its microdrama platform launched in 2024. The company currently produces more than 150 microdramas a month as it expands its content pipeline.
On the cost side, marketing and advertising remained Kuku’s largest expense at Rs 1,105 crore in FY26, nearly four times the Rs 284.8 crore spent in the previous fiscal year. Employee benefit expenses increased 24% to Rs 74.1 crore, which included Rs 18.5 crore ESOP cost.
IT expenses more than doubled to Rs 56.7 crore, while operational costs surged to Rs 96.25 crore from Rs 8.65 crore, and payment gateway charges increased to Rs 43.2 crore. Overall, Kuku’s total expenditure rose 3.5X to Rs 1,421.7 crore in FY26 from Rs 411 crore in FY25.
Kuku’s higher marketing spending supported its sharp revenue growth, helping the company absorb the rise in expenses and swing to a net profit of Rs 182.7 crore in FY26 from a loss of Rs 152.6 crore in FY25. Its profit before tax stood at Rs 88.6 crore, while a deferred tax benefit of Rs 98.1 crore boosted its bottom line.
Its EBITDA stood at Rs 82.9 crore with a margin of 5.6%, compared with an EBITDA loss of Rs 159.8 crore in FY25.

The company’s cash and bank balance also increased 2.5X to Rs 293 crore at the end of FY26, while current assets rose to Rs 746 crore.
Ahead of its proposed Rs 3,500 crore IPO, Kuku is also building a 1,000-member AI-led content production unit to scale its microdrama business. The company plans to use AI across writing, production, post-production, dubbing and localisation as it looks to increase content output while reducing production costs. The company said 60-70% of its content already uses AI tools at different stages of production. Kuku also spends over Rs 200 crore annually on content and works with a creator ecosystem of around 50,000 people.
Kuku’s next phase will depend on whether its microdrama bet can sustain the momentum beyond an initial surge in demand. The format faces challenges around the high cost of producing fresh, short-form content, retaining subscribers amid low switching costs, and maintaining engagement as audiences have a steady stream of competing content. Kuku’s push toward AI-led production could help improve the economics, but scaling output without diluting content quality will remain a key test as the company builds a larger content business.

title: Indian startups raise $2.9 Bn in Q3 2026 as EV, AI drive funding
summary:
Indian startups raised less than $3 billion in funding in Q3 2026, down from $3.5 billion in Q2 and $3.87 billion in Q1. The quarter saw fewer large funding rounds, with Simple Energy leading the pack with a $182 million raise. The round also made Simple Energy the third-largest funded Indian electric two-wheeler OEM. Physical AI startup SiMa.ai, which has deep Indian roots and a major research and development centre in Bengaluru, raised another $150 million. Emergent, River Mobility, Navi, Slice and Pixxel also secured more than $100 million each during the quarter.

Despite the decline in overall funding, early-stage deals crossed the $1 billion mark in Q3. The quarter also saw six startup listings, including NSE, Rentomojo, Molbio, Milky Mist, Leap India and Purple Style Labs. Six startups shut down operations during the quarter.
[Overview]
According to data compiled by Entrackr, Indian startups raised approximately $2.9 billion in funding during the third quarter of 2026. This amount included 46 growth and late-stage deals totalling $1.89 billion, along with 194 early-stage deals worth $1.01 billion. Additionally, there were 26 undisclosed deals during the period.
[Q-o-Q and M-o-M trend]
Q3 2026 saw a modest recovery in startup funding compared to the same quarter last year. Total funding rose to $2.9 billion from $2.78 billion in Q3 2025, but remained below the $4 billion recorded in Q3 2024. September emerged as a strong month for funding, as startups raised more than $1 billion for the third time in 2026. February and June were the previous two months to cross the $1 billion mark, with each recording around $2 billion in funding. The September uptick helped Q3 close above the funding level recorded in the year-ago quarter.

[Top 15 growth-stage deals]
In Q3 2026, India’s top 15 growth and late-stage deals reflected strong investor interest in mobility, AI and fintech, along with bets across consumer and deeptech sectors. Simple Energy topped the list after raising $182 million in its Series C round, followed by physical AI startup SiMa.ai, which secured $150 million in Series C funding. AI startup Emergent raised $130 million, while electric two-wheeler maker River Mobility secured $120 million. Fintech firms Navi and Slice raised $100 million each, while electric mobility platform Yulu followed with $93 million. EV maker Ultraviolette raised $85 million, while AI startups Ema and Sarvam AI secured $77 million and $74 million, respectively. Wearable tech startup Ultrahuman raised $70 million, while The Pizza Bakery secured $56 million. Healthtech startup Nua raised $50 million, followed by Third Wave Coffee at $43 million and aerospace and defence company Raghu Vamsi Aerospace Group at $40 million.

[Top 15 early-stage deals]
Early-stage activity remained strong in Q3 2026, led by Pixxel’s $100 million Series A and Airbound’s $37 million Series A. Yuma Energy followed with $35 million, while Centricity and InRisk Labs raised $30 million and $27 million, respectively. Most of the top deals fell in the $15–25 million range, reflecting steady investor interest in early-stage companies.

Spacetech, fintech, deeptech and mobility featured prominently among the top deals. Data centre startup CtrlS raised $25 million, while foodtech firm Arboreal Bioinnovations secured $24 million. Business Nextgen Finance and Runable raised $21.7 million and $21 million, respectively. NeoGeo, Nexedge Capital and QNu Labs raised $20 million each, while Gravity, Piston and Plaza rounded out the list at $15 million each.
[Mergers and acquisitions]
The Indian startup ecosystem saw 33 merger and acquisition transactions in Q3 2026, covering sectors such as fintech, healthtech, AI, edtech, spacetech and e-commerce. Some of the notable deals included Samara Capital’s $120 million acquisition of stakes in Associated Road Carriers and Calyx Container Terminal, ITC’s $65 million acquisition of Yoga Bar and Udaan’s $52 million acquisition of Swiggy’s supply chain platform Lynk. Aurum PropTech agreed to acquire Housing.com’s parent in a $46.2 million share swap deal, while Ananta Capital acquired a majority stake in Phitku for $10.6 million. PhysicsWallah also acquired a controlling stake in Sarrthi IAS for $7.5 million. The quarter also saw strategic deals such as InsuranceDekho’s merger with RenewBuy, Adobe’s acquisition of AI startup Rilo and GalaxEye’s acquisition of spacecraft engineering company StarOps.
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru remained the leading startup hub in Q3 2026, accounting for 143 deals worth $2.1 billion, or 72.52% of total funding. Delhi NCR followed with 56 deals worth $296.76 million, while Mumbai recorded 31 deals worth $283.3 million. Pune and Hyderabad ranked next with 11 and seven deals, respectively.

AI led Q3 2026 funding activity with $635.3 million, followed by EV startups at $583 million. Fintech ranked third with $487.7 million, while e-commerce startups raised $222 million. Deeptech and healthtech followed with $123 million and $103 million, respectively.
[Series-wise deals]
Series C deals led Q3 2026 funding, with 11 rounds worth $887 million, accounting for 30.51% of total funding. Series A followed with 59 deals worth $689.17 million, while Series B deals raised $506.2 million across 19 rounds. Seed-stage startups recorded the highest deal count at 88, but raised $174.7 million during the quarter.

[Layoffs, shutdowns and departures]
Layoffs continued across Indian startups and the wider tech ecosystem in Q3 2026, as companies focused on cost optimisation and profitability. Even Healthcare saw the largest workforce reduction, with around 350 employees affected, followed by listed company Zomato, which laid off 270 employees. Uber India also cut around 250 jobs during the quarter.
The quarter also saw six startups shut down: The Ayurveda Co, SatvaKart, Dream Money, Klydo, PicSee and Medial.
Meanwhile, the startup ecosystem recorded 10 senior executive departures across roles such as CEO, CBO, co-founder, managing director and president. The quarter also saw 85 key hires across the ecosystem.
[Trends]
UPI MDR: The return of discussions around interchange or MDR on UPI could reshape the economics of digital payments, particularly for banks and fintech platforms.
Apple Pay enters UPI: Apple’s entry into India’s UPI ecosystem could add a new global player to the country’s digital payments market and increase competition among payment apps.
AceVector IPO: AceVector is set to become the second e-commerce marketplace after Meesho to tap the public markets, pointing to renewed IPO activity in the segment.
EV funding: EV funding rose to $583 million in Q3 2026, driven by major rounds raised by electric two-wheeler makers Simple Energy, River Mobility and Ultraviolette.
Microdrama heats up: Pocket FM re-entered the microdrama segment, while Flipkart recently made its entry. The space already includes Kuku TV, Quick TV, StoryTV and EloTV, while mainstream players such as Yash Raj Films and Sun TV Network have also announced plans to enter microdrama production.
[Conclusion]
Overall, Q3 2026 reflected a mixed quarter for the Indian startup ecosystem, with total funding remaining below the levels seen in the first half of the year despite a recovery from the year-ago quarter. Large rounds were concentrated in EV, AI and fintech, while early-stage funding remained resilient. At the same time, IPO activity, M&A transactions and developments across UPI, EVs and microdrama added to the quarter’s activity despite tighter funding conditions.

title: IPV leads Rs 7 Cr seed round in cybersecurity startup Zaperon
summary:

The fresh funds will be used to advance product capabilities, launch enterprise-grade AI security frameworks and expand its presence in India and the US, Zaperon said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2021 by Vineet Gupta and Sachin Aggarwal, Zaperon is a cybersecurity firm that builds products to protect enterprises from data breaches. It offers a platform-centric approach to enterprise security that allows organisations to secure their entire IT landscape through a single Zaperon console.
By bringing together identity security, data security and AI governance, Zaperon enables enterprises to control how users, applications and AI agents access and interact with sensitive data and cloud infrastructure. The platform aims to replace fragmented security controls with consistent, identity and context-aware policies across digital and AI environments.
According to market research, identity security and data security represent an estimated $16 billion global opportunity today, which is projected to reach $35 billion by 2030.
The Delhi-based startup’s enterprise client base spans banking and financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, technology and government sectors, where protecting sensitive data and controlling access to critical systems are key security and compliance requirements.
Indian cybersecurity startups raised $89 million across 17 funding rounds in H1 2026, nearly double the $47 million raised in H1 2025.
Recent deals include QNu Labs, which raised Rs 200 crore in a Series A1 round led by the National Quantum Mission and Speciale Invest to scale its quantum-safe cybersecurity solutions; Mitigata, which secured $15 million in Series B funding led by Bessemer Venture Partners for its AI-powered cyber-resilience platform; and CloudSEK, which raised $10 million from Connecticut Innovations to expand its AI-driven cyber-intelligence platform.
Other startups such as Deep Algorithm Solutions, Equal, Protectt.ai and Astra Security have also raised funding in recent periods, reflecting activity across fraud prevention, identity management, mobile security and cloud penetration testing.

title: Niyo’s income jumps 78% to Rs 178 Cr in FY26
summary:
Travel fintech platform Niyo’s income grew 78% year-on-year to Rs 178 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 100 crore in FY25, according to the company’s press release.
The company also cut its losses by 58% to Rs 33 crore in FY26 from Rs 78 crore a year earlier. Niyo said the improvement came from better efficiency, including the use of AI in customer service, operations, marketing and product development.
Niyo’s operating expenses rose 20% to Rs 201 crore in FY26 from Rs 168 crore in FY25. Employee expenses increased 17% to Rs 92 crore from Rs 79 crore. According to Niyo, the increase in employee costs was mainly due to the expansion of Kanji Forex, which operates under Niyo’s own AD-II licence. 
Despite the higher spending, Niyo’s EBITDA loss nearly halved to Rs 32 crore in FY26 from Rs 77 crore in FY25, the press release added.
Niyo is also expanding beyond its core travel business. The company said its revenue is now coming from forex cash, remittances, flights, hotels, experiences, international eSIMs and insurance, among other services. It is also selling more forex and travel products to its existing customers.
The company has set up Finnew Global Solutions IFSC in GIFT City and received approval to operate as a Payment Service Provider under IFSCA rules.
Niyo CFO Gourav Kumar said the company is now focused on getting more value from its existing customers, improving efficiency and moving towards profitability. Niyo expects to maintain over 50% annual growth in the coming years and become EBITDA positive.
Niyo has raised over $160 million in funding to date, including a $100 million Series C round in 2022. Its investors include Accel, Lightrock, Prime Ventures, Horizon, Tencent, and others.
